jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Operations Planning
jobs.description:
S'more About The Team

The Operations Data and Decisions Tribe at HelloFresh is responsible for driving operations planning by creating high quality, reusable data assets, data science models, and algorithmic solutions. Additionally, the tribe. This team has a direct impact on the customer experience and is constantly optimising for various Business KPIs. They build in-house products using modern technologies to handle a massive scale of transactions (>8.5 million active customers) and continuously improve the SDLC for fast flow and continuous delivery.

As a Director of Operations Planning Engineering, you will lead engineering teams (Data Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, & Analytics) and Staff Engineers across the mid-term planning domain, supporting their technical decision-making processes. Your responsibilities will include spearheading initiatives that traverse multiple teams and domains, such as those focused on network planning, demand planning, and production planning. Drawing upon your comprehensive understanding of the domain, you will own the planning architecture strategy and drive the long-term vision for how our planning systems should be integrated and scaled.

Lettuce Share What This Role Will Be Responsible For

Lead an engineering squad comprising 10-15 engineers, managing Engineering Managers and Staff Engineers across Warsaw, Berlin, & USA.
Own the GenAI transformation — define and drive a concrete roadmap for becoming a genuinely AI-native engineering organisation: from AI-assisted development and automated incident response, to agentic workflows and LLM-powered tooling embedded in day-to-day operations.
Own the availability and reliability of HelloFresh's planning infrastructure — drive SRE practices, incident management, SLOs/SLIs, and on-call maturity across high-throughput systems serving multiple markets.
Set technical direction across Python, GoLang, PostgreSQL, Kafka, React, and React Native services on AWS, ensuring systems.
Partner with Product, Operations, Marketing, and Procurement providers to align engineering priorities with business outcomes.
Manage, coach, and develop Engineering Managers & Engineers — holding them accountable for team health, delivery, and engineering standards.
Navigate organisational change with maturity, keeping teams focused and motivated through evolving priorities.

Sound a-peeling? Here's what we're looking for

AI proficiency and advocacy. Hands-on familiarity with AI technologies and a demonstrable track record of championing their adoption — whether through AI-assisted development workflows, LLM-powered tooling, or driving team-wide GenAI-native ways of working.
Deep Technical Expertise. Mastery of a broad range of technical skills relevant to Operations Planning — including planning systems, data science modeling, data engineering, database systems, distributed computing, and backend development frameworks. Hands-on familiarity with full stack application development.
Systems Thinking. The ability to understand complex systems holistically, recognising how components interact and impact each other, and leveraging this to design scalable, resilient solutions in a high-throughput environment where downtime means direct revenue loss.
Proven Leadership at Scale. 10+ years in software engineering with 4+ years managing Engineering Managers — not just individual contributors. Demonstrated ability to lead distributed teams across multiple offices, building trust and maintaining high engineering standards without daily co-location.
Operational Excellence Mindset. Strong grounding in SRE practices — SLOs/SLIs, incident management, on-call culture, and observability tooling (Grafana or similar). Experience owning payments infrastructure in regulated, multi-market environments is a strong plus.
Cross-Functional Collaboration. Exceptional ability to work across engineering disciplines, Product, business stakeholders, and external service providers — fostering alignment towards common goals and translating business outcomes into engineering priorities.
Effective Communication Across Disciplines. Strong ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences, from engineers to senior business stakeholders.
Low ego, high ownership, and a bias toward clarity over complexity.

Let’s cut to the cheese, this is why you'll love it here

Shape the future of food: Play a key role in transforming how millions of people eat as we grow into a global food solutions company.
Drive transformational change: Your decisions will have a direct and immediate impact, helping to shape strategy, scale teams, and redefine leadership in a rapidly evolving business.
Build a global brand: Create deeper, more sustainable connections with our customers, putting them at the heart of every decision.
Compensation & Financial Wellbeing: Enjoy amazing discounts: 75% off weekly HelloFresh/Chefs Plate meal kits plus 50% off weekly Factor meal boxes.
Health & Wellbeing: Benefit from health and dental coverage from day one, a Health Spending Account, unlimited Headspace access, and 25% off GoodLife fitness memberships.
Flexibility & Work-Life: Receive generous vacation and PTO offerings. Benefit from a parental leave top-up program designed to support expectant parents.
Career & Development: Grow with dedicated L&D initiatives and career support, aligning with our "Learning Never Stops" value.

Flexible Hybrid Approach

At HelloFresh, we know that flexible work arrangements are essential in enabling you to do your best work, while balancing your personal and life needs. Offering remote work flexibility, along with the opportunity to interact and collaborate in the office are all a part of creating a great employee experience.

To meet these needs, we are pleased to provide Flexible Hybrid work. Flexible Hybrid is a people-first approach that is based on choice, trust, personalization, and empowers teams to choose when and how often they work from the office and work from home, in addition to team days and company days. This means a minimum of 2 days in office per week, with most teams in office between 2-3 days a week.

HelloFresh Canada uses AI-integrated technology to help us process and evaluate applications more efficiently. This includes tools that screen and assess candidate qualifications based on the requirements for this role. While these tools assist our workflow, all final selection decisions are made by our hiring team.

Toronto, ON Pay Range

$174,300—$184,300 CAD

jobs.title: Director of Product, Content Intelligence & Growth
jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

The team

Content is the foundation of everything we build at Scribd, Inc. Our UGC corpus—more than 400 million user-uploaded documents, distinct from the rights-protected premium catalogs behind Everand and Fable—powers the consumer experience on Scribd and Slideshare and differentiates our search and discovery.

The Content pillar is the team responsible for that asset. It spans three connected areas—trust & safety (protecting the corpus), understanding (knowing it), and supply (growing it)—each with dedicated product and engineering leadership, embedded analysts, and applied ML capability.

We have high standards, give real feedback, and always bias toward action. Everyone owns their work end-to-end. There's high trust, low hand-holding, and a genuine expectation that you'll push the people around you toward sharper thinking and better outcomes.

We celebrate wins, learn from our losses, and laugh through both.

Join us!

The role

We're hiring a Director of Content Intelligence & Supply to own knowing our UGC corpus and growing it as an asset. This is a new role, and it comes at a moment when content has become central to our strategy: the UGC corpus powers our consumer products and feeds search and discovery.

You'll bring content intelligence and content supply under one point of leadership—connecting what we know about the corpus (classification, metadata, quality, gaps) with the decisions about how we grow it. Today those efforts run in different parts of the org; your job is to run them as one portfolio with one roadmap. We build products that turn information into understanding, grounded in trusted human-created sources—and we own the data structure and intelligence that make a corpus this large useful.

This role reports to the Chief Product Officer. You'll inherit an established team—a content understanding program with its own charter and dedicated engineering squad, and a UGC supply squad that owns the end-to-end contributor experience—with room to shape the org's direction, structure, and future growth.

We're looking for a product leader with real data fluency: probably not a traditional consumer product manager, but someone with a foot in the data science world—as comfortable interrogating a classification model as running a product review—who gets excited about turning a 400-million-document UGC corpus into a strategic asset.

Know the corpus

Own the content understanding roadmap: classification, enrichment, metadata, and quality across the UGC corpus.
Drive corpus gap analysis: where the corpus is deep, where it's thin, and how user-generated and partner content behave differently.
Make the corpus legible—to our own products (search, discovery, recommendations) and to the teams and systems that build on it.
Set direction for classification and corpus-analysis work with credibility, in close partnership with applied ML, engineering, and data science teams.

Grow the supply

Own UGC supply end to end: uploads, conversions, and the supply-side user experience. The people who add content to our platforms are your customer.
Unify content acquisition strategy: set priorities across user-generated supply, partnerships, and other related programs that today run independently—coordinating the strategy while execution stays with the teams closest to it.
Connect supply to demand: partner with the consumer product orgs so the corpus grows where it creates the most value for readers, learners, and subscribers.

Build the knowledge infrastructure for AI

Own the AI product foundation of our UGC corpus: segmentation, sampling, corpus description, and the metadata and retrieval capabilities. The scope is the UGC corpus only: content in our premium catalogs is not part of it.
Partner with business development on evolving corpus intelligence needs.

Lead and develop the team

Lead senior product leaders and an established program with its own charter, engineering squads, and embedded analysts.
Step into a team with strong people already in seat: earn trust quickly, raise the bar, and multiply the leaders around you.
Operate as a peer among directors and VPs: represent content strategy in executive conversations with clarity and confidence, and connect corpus decisions to business outcomes.

The Essentials

10+ years of product management experience, including 4+ years leading product teams or senior PMs.
Depth in data-heavy product domains: ML/AI-powered products, search, recommendations, content platforms, or marketplaces.
Genuine data fluency—you can credibly direct classification and corpus-analysis work and partner with applied ML and data science teams as an equal, even if you don't build the models yourself.
Familiarity with common data structures around the use of content for AI training.
Experience with supply-side or two-sided product dynamics: creators, contributors, sellers, or content acquisition.
A strategic operator who connects content decisions to business outcomes—licensing revenue, product quality, growth—and can hold a portfolio-level roadmap.
Strong communication and cross-functional leadership: comfortable operating with executives and setting priorities across teams you don't manage.
Experience with content licensing or B2B data products is a plus.

The application

Resume.
Optional: anything that shows how you think about content, data, or supply—writing, a talk, or a product/strategy artifact you're proud of.

At Scribd, Inc., your base pay is one part of your total compensation package and is determined within a range. Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location. San Francisco is our highest geographic market in the United States.

In the state of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $214,000 [minimum salary in our lowest geographic market within California] to $280,000 [maximum salary in our highest geographic market within California].

In the United States, outside of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $203,000 [minimum salary in our lowest US geographic market outside of California] to $270,000 [maximum salary in our highest US geographic market outside of California].

In Canada, the reasonably expected salary range is between $190,000 CAD[minimum salary in our lowest geographic market] to $250,000 CAD[maximum salary in our highest geographic market].

We carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including but not limited to experience; job-related skill sets; relevant education or training; and other business and organizational needs. The salary range listed is for the level at which this job has been scoped. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for a competitive equity ownership, and a comprehensive and generous benefits package.

Working at Scribd, Inc.

one of the following cities. This includes surrounding metro areas or locations within a typical commuting distance:

Scribd Flex (flexible work model)
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
Mental health support and disability coverage
Generous paid time off, including vacation, sick time, holidays, winter break, volunteer time, and sabbaticals
Paid parental leave and family support benefits
Retirement matching and employee equity
Learning and development programs and professional growth opportunities

Complimentary access to the Scribd, Inc. suite of products
Enterprise access to leading AI tools

Get to Know Scribd, Inc.

About Scribd, Inc.

Life at Scribd, Inc.

We want our interview process to be accessible to everyone. You can inform us of any reasonable adjustments we can make to better accommodate your needs by emailing accommodations@scribd.com about the need for adjustments at any point in the interview process.

If you apply for a job with Scribd, Inc. or otherwise engage with us in connection with employment (including as an employee, contractor, or other personnel), the personal information we process in that context is subject to our Employee and Applicant Privacy Policy, which is available here .

Scribd, Inc. is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We encourage people of all backgrounds to apply, and believe that a diversity of perspectives and experiences create a foundation for the best ideas. Come join us in building something meaningful.

new_jobs.description:
S'more About The Team

The Operations Data and Decisions Tribe at HelloFresh is responsible for driving operations planning by creating high quality, reusable data assets, data science models, and algorithmic solutions. Additionally, the tribe. This team has a direct impact on the customer experience and is constantly optimising for various Business KPIs. They build in-house products using modern technologies to handle a massive scale of transactions (>8.5 million active customers) and continuously improve the SDLC for fast flow and continuous delivery.

As a Director of Operations Planning Engineering, you will lead engineering teams (Data Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, & Analytics) and Staff Engineers across the mid-term planning domain, supporting their technical decision-making processes. Your responsibilities will include spearheading initiatives that traverse multiple teams and domains, such as those focused on network planning, demand planning, and production planning. Drawing upon your comprehensive understanding of the domain, you will own the planning architecture strategy and drive the long-term vision for how our planning systems should be integrated and scaled.

Lettuce Share What This Role Will Be Responsible For

Lead an engineering squad comprising 10-15 engineers, managing Engineering Managers and Staff Engineers across Warsaw, Berlin, & USA.
Own the GenAI transformation — define and drive a concrete roadmap for becoming a genuinely AI-native engineering organisation: from AI-assisted development and automated incident response, to agentic workflows and LLM-powered tooling embedded in day-to-day operations.
Own the availability and reliability of HelloFresh's planning infrastructure — drive SRE practices, incident management, SLOs/SLIs, and on-call maturity across high-throughput systems serving multiple markets.
Set technical direction across Python, GoLang, PostgreSQL, Kafka, React, and React Native services on AWS, ensuring systems.
Partner with Product, Operations, Marketing, and Procurement providers to align engineering priorities with business outcomes.
Manage, coach, and develop Engineering Managers & Engineers — holding them accountable for team health, delivery, and engineering standards.
Navigate organisational change with maturity, keeping teams focused and motivated through evolving priorities.

Sound a-peeling? Here's what we're looking for

AI proficiency and advocacy. Hands-on familiarity with AI technologies and a demonstrable track record of championing their adoption — whether through AI-assisted development workflows, LLM-powered tooling, or driving team-wide GenAI-native ways of working.
Deep Technical Expertise. Mastery of a broad range of technical skills relevant to Operations Planning — including planning systems, data science modeling, data engineering, database systems, distributed computing, and backend development frameworks. Hands-on familiarity with full stack application development.
Systems Thinking. The ability to understand complex systems holistically, recognising how components interact and impact each other, and leveraging this to design scalable, resilient solutions in a high-throughput environment where downtime means direct revenue loss.
Proven Leadership at Scale. 10+ years in software engineering with 4+ years managing Engineering Managers — not just individual contributors. Demonstrated ability to lead distributed teams across multiple offices, building trust and maintaining high engineering standards without daily co-location.
Operational Excellence Mindset. Strong grounding in SRE practices — SLOs/SLIs, incident management, on-call culture, and observability tooling (Grafana or similar). Experience owning payments infrastructure in regulated, multi-market environments is a strong plus.
Cross-Functional Collaboration. Exceptional ability to work across engineering disciplines, Product, business stakeholders, and external service providers — fostering alignment towards common goals and translating business outcomes into engineering priorities.
Effective Communication Across Disciplines. Strong ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences, from engineers to senior business stakeholders.
Low ego, high ownership, and a bias toward clarity over complexity.

Let’s cut to the cheese, this is why you'll love it here

Shape the future of food: Play a key role in transforming how millions of people eat as we grow into a global food solutions company.
Drive transformational change: Your decisions will have a direct and immediate impact, helping to shape strategy, scale teams, and redefine leadership in a rapidly evolving business.
Build a global brand: Create deeper, more sustainable connections with our customers, putting them at the heart of every decision.
Compensation & Financial Wellbeing: Enjoy amazing discounts: 75% off weekly HelloFresh/Chefs Plate meal kits plus 50% off weekly Factor meal boxes.
Health & Wellbeing: Benefit from health and dental coverage from day one, a Health Spending Account, unlimited Headspace access, and 25% off GoodLife fitness memberships.
Flexibility & Work-Life: Receive generous vacation and PTO offerings. Benefit from a parental leave top-up program designed to support expectant parents.
Career & Development: Grow with dedicated L&D initiatives and career support, aligning with our "Learning Never Stops" value.

At HelloFresh, we know that flexible work arrangements are essential in enabling you to do your best work, while balancing your personal and life needs. Offering remote work flexibility, along with the opportunity to interact and collaborate in the office are all a part of creating a great employee experience.

To meet these needs, we are pleased to provide Flexible Hybrid work. Flexible Hybrid is a people-first approach that is based on choice, trust, personalization, and empowers teams to choose when and how often they work from the office and work from home, in addition to team days and company days. This means a minimum of 2 days in office per week, with most teams in office between 2-3 days a week.

This includes tools that screen and assess candidate qualifications based on the requirements for this role. While these tools assist our workflow, all final selection decisions are made by our hiring team.

new_jobs.title: Director of Product, Content Intelligence & Growth
new_jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

Culture at Scribd, Inc.

We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

The team

Content is the foundation of everything we build at Scribd, Inc. Our UGC corpus—more than 400 million user-uploaded documents, distinct from the rights-protected premium catalogs behind Everand and Fable—powers the consumer experience on Scribd and Slideshare and differentiates our search and discovery.

The Content pillar is the team responsible for that asset. It spans three connected areas—trust & safety (protecting the corpus), understanding (knowing it), and supply (growing it)—each with dedicated product and engineering leadership, embedded analysts, and applied ML capability.

We have high standards, give real feedback, and always bias toward action. Everyone owns their work end-to-end. There's high trust, low hand-holding, and a genuine expectation that you'll push the people around you toward sharper thinking and better outcomes.

We celebrate wins, learn from our losses, and laugh through both.

Join us!

The role

We're hiring a Director of Content Intelligence & Supply to own knowing our UGC corpus and growing it as an asset. This is a new role, and it comes at a moment when content has become central to our strategy: the UGC corpus powers our consumer products and feeds search and discovery.

You'll bring content intelligence and content supply under one point of leadership—connecting what we know about the corpus (classification, metadata, quality, gaps) with the decisions about how we grow it. Today those efforts run in different parts of the org; your job is to run them as one portfolio with one roadmap. We build products that turn information into understanding, grounded in trusted human-created sources—and we own the data structure and intelligence that make a corpus this large useful.

This role reports to the Chief Product Officer. You'll inherit an established team—a content understanding program with its own charter and dedicated engineering squad, and a UGC supply squad that owns the end-to-end contributor experience—with room to shape the org's direction, structure, and future growth.

We're looking for a product leader with real data fluency: probably not a traditional consumer product manager, but someone with a foot in the data science world—as comfortable interrogating a classification model as running a product review—who gets excited about turning a 400-million-document UGC corpus into a strategic asset.

Know the corpus

Own the content understanding roadmap: classification, enrichment, metadata, and quality across the UGC corpus.
Drive corpus gap analysis: where the corpus is deep, where it's thin, and how user-generated and partner content behave differently.
Make the corpus legible—to our own products (search, discovery, recommendations) and to the teams and systems that build on it.
Set direction for classification and corpus-analysis work with credibility, in close partnership with applied ML, engineering, and data science teams.

Grow the supply

Own UGC supply end to end: uploads, conversions, and the supply-side user experience. The people who add content to our platforms are your customer.
Unify content acquisition strategy: set priorities across user-generated supply, partnerships, and other related programs that today run independently—coordinating the strategy while execution stays with the teams closest to it.
Connect supply to demand: partner with the consumer product orgs so the corpus grows where it creates the most value for readers, learners, and subscribers.

Build the knowledge infrastructure for AI

Own the AI product foundation of our UGC corpus: segmentation, sampling, corpus description, and the metadata and retrieval capabilities. The scope is the UGC corpus only: content in our premium catalogs is not part of it.
Partner with business development on evolving corpus intelligence needs.

Lead and develop the team

Lead senior product leaders and an established program with its own charter, engineering squads, and embedded analysts.
Step into a team with strong people already in seat: earn trust quickly, raise the bar, and multiply the leaders around you.
Operate as a peer among directors and VPs: represent content strategy in executive conversations with clarity and confidence, and connect corpus decisions to business outcomes.

The Essentials

10+ years of product management experience, including 4+ years leading product teams or senior PMs.
Depth in data-heavy product domains: ML/AI-powered products, search, recommendations, content platforms, or marketplaces.
Genuine data fluency—you can credibly direct classification and corpus-analysis work and partner with applied ML and data science teams as an equal, even if you don't build the models yourself.
Familiarity with common data structures around the use of content for AI training.
Experience with supply-side or two-sided product dynamics: creators, contributors, sellers, or content acquisition.
A strategic operator who connects content decisions to business outcomes—licensing revenue, product quality, growth—and can hold a portfolio-level roadmap.
Strong communication and cross-functional leadership: comfortable operating with executives and setting priorities across teams you don't manage.
Experience with content licensing or B2B data products is a plus.

The application

Resume.
Optional: anything that shows how you think about content, data, or supply—writing, a talk, or a product/strategy artifact you're proud of.

At Scribd, Inc., your base pay is one part of your total compensation package and is determined within a range. Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location. San Francisco is our highest geographic market in the United States.

In the state of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $214,000 [minimum salary in our lowest geographic market within California] to $280,000 [maximum salary in our highest geographic market within California].

In the United States, outside of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $203,000 [minimum salary in our lowest US geographic market outside of California] to $270,000 [maximum salary in our highest US geographic market outside of California].

In Canada, the reasonably expected salary range is between $190,000 CAD[minimum salary in our lowest geographic market] to $250,000 CAD[maximum salary in our highest geographic market].

We carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including but not limited to experience; job-related skill sets; relevant education or training; and other business and organizational needs. The salary range listed is for the level at which this job has been scoped. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for a competitive equity ownership, and a comprehensive and generous benefits package.
